---
title: Invoice disputes
department: finance
status: archived
---
An invoice dispute is raised when a customer believes a charge on their invoice
is wrong. It is distinct from a refund, which follows a service failure that both
parties already agree happened.

A dispute must be raised within thirty days of the invoice date. After thirty
days the invoice is treated as accepted and the only remaining route is a
commercial gesture agreed by the account manager, which is recorded differently
in the ledger and does not affect the disputed invoice.

Raising a dispute suspends the disputed lines only. The undisputed balance
remains payable on the original terms, and a customer who withholds the whole
invoice while disputing one line will still receive a dunning notice for the
remainder.

The most common dispute categories are a surcharge the customer did not expect, a
chargeable weight that differs from the weight the customer declared, and a
delivery attempt billed as a second attempt when the first attempt was not made.

Chargeable weight disputes are resolved against the dimensioning scanner record,
which stores the measured dimensions and a photograph of the parcel on the belt.
Where no scanner record exists the customer's declared weight is accepted.

Disputes are acknowledged within two business days and resolved within fifteen.
A dispute unresolved at fifteen business days escalates to the finance duty
manager, and one unresolved at thirty escalates to the finance director.

Credit notes issued to settle a dispute reference the original invoice number and
the disputed line. A credit note without that reference cannot be reconciled by
the customer's accounts payable team and generates a second dispute, which is
why the reference is mandatory rather than best practice.
